related_questions.question: How to pay child support in Montana?

text_blocks.snippet: In Montana, child support payments can be made through various methods, including online, by mail, in person, or through electronic funds transfer. The Montana Department of Health and Human Services, Child Support Services Division (CSSD) manages child support payments and provides several options for making payments.
snippet_highlighted_words: online, by mail, in person, or through electronic funds transfer

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of the payment options:

list.snippet: The OPP allows payments from a checking or savings account or with a credit/debit card.
A transaction fee of 1.5% of the payment amount applies, with a maximum of $20.00, plus an additional variable fee for credit/debit card payments.
Only Visa, MasterCard, Discover, and American Express credit/debit cards are accepted.
The OPP works best with Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge browsers.
Payments can be mailed to the CSSD using a money order or check (make checks payable to CSSD).
The address for mailing payments is: CSSD, PO Box 5200, Helena, MT 59604-5200.
Include the participant's name, case number, and the amount of the payment.
Payments can be made in person at the Missoula County Clerk of District Court's office (200 West Broadway, 2nd floor, Courthouse).
Accepted payment methods include cash, money order, and credit/debit cards (Visa, Mastercard, and Discover).
Personal checks, cashier's checks, and American Express are not accepted.
Employers can set up EFT to automatically transmit child support payments through the ACH network.
This option is also available for individuals who want to make payments directly from their bank accounts.
The CSSD also offers payment options through Direct Deposit and Reliacard, which may not be immediately reflected in the account balance.
The CSSD recommends contacting the bank or Reliacard provider to verify the balance and avoid overdraft fees.
If you are receiving income withholding orders electronically (e-IWO), the federal e-IWO process can be used to save time and money.
When making online payments, ensure you only click the submit button once to avoid multiple deductions from your bank account or credit card.
If you experience any issues with online payments, contact the CSSD help desk immediately.
Child support payments are not distributed to the CSSD until the funds have cleared your bank or are guaranteed by your credit card company, which may take several days.
For any questions or concerns regarding child support payments, contact the CSSD directly.

related_questions.snippet: The higher the parenting time total, the lower the child support amount. The nonresidential parent pays child support to the residential parent. In the case of an approximate 50/50 split in parenting time, the higher earner pays child support to the lower earner.
